page.title: SpringSaLaD Results
page.introduction: A finished SpringSaLaD simulation produces two different kinds of result, and the results window has a tab for each. View Data holds the counters - how many molecules, how many bound sites, how the numbers change over time. 3D Trajectory holds the positions - every particle, at every stored snapshot, in the box it moved through.
page.appearance:
Which tabs appear depends on what the run produced:
View Data - always. Its contents differ between a single trajectory and multiple runs, described below.
3D Trajectory - whenever the dataset carries stored snapshots, which is any Langevin run.
Langevin Clusters - only when cluster tracking produced data.
page.operations:
View Data, after a single trajectory. The ordinary plot and spreadsheet, over the counters the solver wrote rather than over observables. For each molecule there are three: TOTAL_, FREE_ and BOUND_, and each state of each site is counted the same way. The Plot / Data buttons under the graph switch between the curve and the numbers behind it.
View Data, after multiple runs. The tab is replaced by a panel built for comparing runs. On the left, choose what to show:
Molecules, Bound Sites, Free Sites or Total Sites - which family of counters;
Average, Min / Max or Standard Deviation - what to show about the spread across the independent runs.
This is the reason to ask for multiple runs at all. A single stochastic trajectory of a few hundred particles is noisy enough that its shape is not the model's answer; the average over several runs, with the spread drawn around it, is.
Langevin Clusters. When cluster tracking is on, this tab reports how molecules aggregated: Cluster Counts, Cluster Mass, Cluster Mean and Cluster Overall. Cluster tracking generates a lot of data, so it is worth turning on only when aggregation is the question being asked.
The 3D Trajectory viewer. A play-back of the run: every molecule drawn as its sites, joined by its links, inside the simulation box with the membrane drawn as a plane.
Drag to rotate the scene, and use the mouse wheel to zoom. Reset view puts the camera back.
The slider along the bottom steps through the stored snapshots; the readout beside it names the frame and its time. How many snapshots there are is set by the Image Interval in the solver options, not by the output interval.
Play runs through them at the chosen frame rate.
Save movie... writes the sequence out as a video.
Links, Box and Membrane show and hide those parts of the scene.
The Species tree gives every molecule and every one of its sites a checkbox, with All and None beneath. Hiding everything except one site type is the quickest way to see what that site is doing in a crowded box.
A note on colour. The viewer draws on a black background, so sites given a dark colour are hard to see or invisible. Colours are set per site on the Molecular Structures tab, and the reserved Anchor site defaults to DARK_GRAY - which reads perfectly well in the tables and the molecule diagram, and disappears here. If a molecule seems to be missing from the scene, check its colours before its coordinates.
